intro.name: The monument
intro.text:
For many years, the village has been home to a monument of questionable beauty. Some call it an important piece of Isolan history. Others call it the ugliest thing they have ever seen.
The monument is {A}.
{@Chief} announces a competition to improve its appearance. (Builder1) and (builder2) eagerly volunteer.

ask.name: What to do
ask.text:
One wants to {restore the original design|replace the entire thing|cover it with beautiful decorations|repair its structural flaws}. The other wants to {modernize it|make it more practical|preserve every scratch and crack|add something truly spectacular}.
Unfortunately, the villagers cannot agree on whether the monument is ugly, charming, historically important, or all three.
What should {@chief} do?

restore.text: The builders are instructed to repair the monument while preserving its original character. They begin cleaning, measuring, and replacing damaged stones.

free.text: {@Chief} allows the builders to do whatever they think is best. Both look delighted. The villagers begin to worry.

vote.text: {@Chief} calls a public meeting. Everyone is invited to propose improvements, including those who actually LIKE the old monument.

r1.text: The builders discover delicate carvings beneath years of dirt. The monument was beautiful all along!

r2.text: The repairs are completed without incident. The monument still looks rather strange, but it is safe and well maintained.

r3.text: A builder accidentally removes a stone that was holding up the statue's enormous nose. With a terrible CRACK, the nose falls off, rolls down the path, and comes to rest in front of {@chief}. Nobody says a word.

r4.text: The builders discover that the crooked shape was intentional. Apparently, the monument was designed to align with a rare astronomical event. They abandon their plan to straighten it.

r5.text: The restoration reveals that the statue was assembled backward centuries ago. The villagers debate whether to correct it.

f1.text: The builders produce a magnificent masterpiece. Even their harshest critics are impressed.

f2.text: The monument is covered in so many decorations that nobody can tell what it used to be. The children love it.

f3.text: One builder adds a fountain. The other adds a second fountain. The resulting structure resembles a stone creature with a spectacularly runny nose.

f4.text: The builders accidentally make the monument even uglier. To everyone's surprise, the villagers grow rather fond of it.

f5.text: The builders argue over every detail and refuse to cooperate. {@Chief} separates their work into two competing proposals.

f6.text: The monument looks wonderful, but the new decorations block a frequently used village path. The builders must revise their design before it can be accepted.

v1.text: The majority votes to restore the original. The builders obey, though some villagers are disappointed.

v2.text: The majority votes for a complete redesign. A small group protests that the monument belongs to their ancestors. {@Chief} pauses the work and invites them to help plan it.

v3.text: The vote ends in a perfect tie. {@Chief} {orders another vote|proposes a compromise|decides to leave the monument alone}.

v4.text: A child suggests planting flowers around the monument instead. Everyone realizes this would be cheaper, safer, and rather pretty.

v5.text: The villagers argue for hours. By the end, everyone is so exhausted that they agree to postpone the matter until next year.

nose.name: The nose incident
nose.text:
The great stone nose lies in the middle of the path.
(Builder1) {tries to lift it|apologizes repeatedly|insists that it was already loose}. (Builder2) {stares in disbelief|bursts out laughing|asks whether this technically counts as an improvement}.

final.name: The final presentations
final.text:
(Builder1) unveils {a tasteful restoration|a towering new facade|a modest but sturdy repair|an elegant stone carving}. (Builder2) reveals {a colorful redesign|a practical improvement|a monument covered in tiny sculptures|a surprisingly minimalist design}.
The judges {JUDGING}.

quiet.name: Quiet ending
quiet.text:
The villagers eventually return to their daily routines. Some still think the monument is hideous. Others insist that it has never looked better. A few have already forgotten why anyone was arguing.
But the monument remains, a reminder that beauty is not always something everyone agrees upon.
